bib.title: RAIN: Your Language Models Can Align Themselves without Finetuning

question: Can frozen, unaligned LLMs be aligned to human preferences at inference time, without finetuning or any alignment data?
hypothesis: Following the superficial alignment hypothesis, selecting a sub-distribution of outputs should not need parameter updates, so self-evaluation plus rewind can align a frozen model.
contributions: Rewindable Auto-regressive INference (RAIN): inference-time search with self-evaluation and rewind, no training, gradient computation or parameter updates, no extra data
Experiments on HH, AdvBench, TruthfulQA and IMDB across LLaMA, LLaMA-2, Vicuna, Alpaca, GPT-neo

method.summary: RAIN searches a tree of token sets in an inner loop (PUCT-style forward selection, self-evaluation by the frozen model with a harmless/harmful prompt, similarity-based attribute update, rewind) and an outer loop that picks the next token set by normalised root-child visit counts. Evaluated with GPT-4 and human judges.

datasets.name: IMDB
datasets.preprocessing: initial tokens of a review used as prompt

inference.decoding: RAIN tree search; next token set chosen by normalised visit counts of root children; search stops when score exceeds threshold V or max iterations T
inference.samples: q candidate token sets sampled per expansion; baseline repeated sampling uses 500 samples; number of runs/seeds not stated
inference.prompting: Self-evaluation prompt with A/B option swap (harmless/harmful label order swapped, scores averaged); score -1 harmful, +1 harmless

other.GCG settings: lr 0.01, batch 512, top-k 256, temperature 1, 100 update steps
other.RLAIF baseline: revisions=2; RLHF and RLAIF learning rates 3e-4 (SFT), 5e-4 (RM), 1.4e-5 (RL), warm-up and cosine decay

metrics.name: harmlessness rate
metrics.definition: fraction of responses GPT-4 judges harmless

metrics.name: win rate
metrics.definition: win/(win+loss) vs vanilla, GPT-4, order shuffled

eval.protocol: GPT-4 judge; human eval by 10 annotators on LLaMA2 13B HH, shuffled; no seeds or significance tests stated

prompts.text:
Determine if the assistant's response is harmful. The given conversation should be evaluated solely on its content.
<Generated Text>
Options:
(A) Assistant's response is harmless/harmful.
(B) Assistant's response is harmful/harmless.

[INST] Consider the following question(Q) and answer(A). Determine if the answer is truthful. Answers that are inconsistent with objective facts or are subjectively speculated are considered dishonest.
<Generated Text>
Is the answer truthful? [\INST]

Consider the following movie reviews. Determine if the movie review is positive. If the reviewer likes the movie being reviewed, the review is positive.
<Generated Text>
Options:
(A) The movie review is positive/negative.
(B) The movie review is negative/positive.
(C) The movie review is neutral.

results.claim: RAIN raises LLaMA 30B harmlessness rate on HH from vanilla 82% to 97%, helpfulness maintained
results.setup: HH dataset, LLaMA 30B, GPT-4 judge, frozen model, no training
results.note: Table 5 prints 82.2% and 97.0%; helpfulness shown only in Fig 2 (no numbers)
results.quote: RAIN improves the harmlessness rate of LLaMA 30B from 82% of vanilla inference to 97%, while maintaining the helpfulness rate

results.claim: Repeated cherry-pick sampling (500 samples, chosen by the LLM itself) reaches only 88.1% on LLaMA 30B versus RAIN 97.0%
results.setup: HH, LLaMA 30B, GPT-4 judge, 500 samples picked by LLM self-evaluation

results.claim: On LLaMA 7B repeated sampling gives no gain (64.4% vs 64.4%); RAIN 69.3%
RAIN costs about 4.36x vanilla decode time on LLaMA 30B
results.setup: HH, time ratio = total RAIN time / vanilla time

results.claim: Time ratio on LLaMA 65B and LLaMA-2 70B is 3.95x and 3.78x; overhead shrinks as model is safer
Self-evaluation accuracy of harmfulness is 52% for LLaMA v1 7B and v2 7B
Self-evaluation accuracy 81% at v1 30B, 98% at v2 70B
Under GCG white-box attack, RAIN lowers Vicuna 33B attack success rate from 94% to 19%
results.setup: AdvBench, GCG (lr 0.01, batch 512, top-k 256, temp 1, 100 steps), Vicuna 33B
results.note: Vicuna 7B 86->72, 13B 83->38; transfer 80->55, 79->32, 34->10. Authors do not claim robustness to adaptive attacks

results.claim: On TruthfulQA, RAIN raises LLaMA-2-chat 13B True+Info from 68.5% to 72.8%
results.setup: TruthfulQA, LLaMA-2-chat 13B, two fine-tuned GPT-3 judges
results.note: True 69.2->74.1; Info 98.8->98.6. Abstract says improvement of 5% for truthfulness
results.table: Table 2, row RAIN, column True + Info

results.claim: Positive-sentiment rate on IMDB rises from 62.1% to 82.1% for LLaMA 7B
Ablation: removing similarity update, dynamic node addition, exploration raises ASR from 19% to 22%, 25%, 27%
results.setup: LLaMA-2-chat 13B, GCG white-box on AdvBench; ablations cumulative
results.table: Table 4, row - Exploration encouragement, column ASR

results.claim: Human evaluation: RAIN 96.6% vs vanilla 89.5% harmlessness; GPT-4 98.3% vs 91.1%
RLHF/RLAIF comparison on LLaMA 30B: RAIN efficacy 'comparable, if not superior' (values in Fig 5 only, no numbers printed)
results.setup: HH, LLaMA 30B; RLHF and RLAIF with SFT and SFT+RL; RLAIF revisions=2
results.quote: Compared to RLHF and RLAIF, which require additional data, the efficacy of RAIN is comparable, if not superior.

limits: RAIN needs longer inference time (about 4x on HH); authors suggest generating data with RAIN then finetuning
Robustness only under static LLM-ATTACKS, not adaptive attacks
Dataset sizes, sample counts, seeds, T, Tm, V, q, threshold not stated
Judging is GPT-4 (human eval only on LLaMA2 13B HH); gains small or negative for small models (GPT-neo parity, helpfulness slightly reduced)
RLHF/RLAIF comparison reported only as a figure

terms.definition: Rewindable Auto-regressive INference: search and rewind operations for self-alignment of frozen LLMs in the inference phase
